learning_objective: 🎯 Master the exciting link between chemistry and electricity! Learn how chemical reactions generate power (batteries) and how electricity can force chemical reactions to happen.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: These devices convert chemical energy into electrical energy. A classic example is the Daniel Cell. Oxidation happens at the Anode (loses electrons), and Reduction happens at the Cathode (gains electrons). Remember: 'An Ox and Red Cat'.

Standard cell potentials assume 1M concentrations. The Nernst equation lets you calculate the voltage of a cell at *any* concentration and temperature! It connects the voltage directly to the reaction quotient.
Just like wires, liquid solutions with ions conduct electricity. Molar conductivity usually increases when you dilute a solution because the ions get more space to move around freely.

At infinite dilution, the total molar conductivity of an electrolyte is simply the sum of the individual conductivities of its cations and anions. It's a great tool for finding the conductivity of weak acids!

Here, we use an outside battery to FORCE a non-spontaneous chemical reaction (like splitting water). Faraday's First Law says the mass of a substance deposited at an electrode is directly proportional to the amount of electricity passed.

fun_activity.title: 🍋 The Lemon Battery
fun_activity.instructions: Roll a lemon on a table to juice it inside. Insert a galvanized nail (zinc) into one side and a copper coin into the other. Touch a voltmeter to both metals. The acidic lemon juice acts as an electrolyte, creating a real functioning chemical battery!

exam_tips: 📌 Always remember the convention: In a Galvanic cell, the Anode is Negative and the Cathode is Positive. Electrons flow from Anode to Cathode through the external wire.
📌 When using the Nernst equation, carefully identify the number of electrons transferred ($n$) in the balanced redox equation.
📌 The Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) is assigned an exact potential of 0.00 Volts and is used as the baseline to measure all other elements.
quick_recap: ⭐ Oxidation is loss of electrons; Reduction is gain of electrons (OIL RIG).
⭐ A Salt Bridge keeps the solutions electrically neutral and completes the internal circuit.
⭐ Primary batteries (like clock batteries) cannot be recharged, but secondary batteries (like car batteries or lithium-ion) can!
